newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela privatization head seen soon leaving job.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela privatization head seen soon leaving job.

text.p: Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto, who heads the government privatization program, will leave his job to become Canadian ambassador in September, a well-placed government source said Monday.
"He is going to Canada but it cannot be confirmed officially until the other government gives its go ahead," the source said.
Poletto was formally proposed to the Canadian government two weeks ago but his move, "won't happen before September," the source added.

In a FIV statement responding to a newspaper report, Poletto said he had no plans to leave his current job while moves to privatize state steel and aluminum companies and re-organize the FIV were still pending.
"Obviously this situation (becoming Canadian ambassador) could occur, but it is up to the President of the Republic to take this decision," Poletto was quoted as saying in the FIV release.
Poletto, who replaced former FIV chief Carlos Bernardez in November 1995, has had a mixed term as head of the privatization program.
His office has overseen a $1 billion global issue of the government's 40 percent stake in telephone company CANTV and prepared steel and aluminum companies for privatization later this year.

But the privatization process has constantly fallen behind schedule and a previous privatization success -- international air carrier Viasa -- was closed down earlier this year when the FIV and Spain's Iberia could not work out a rescue package.
Poletto will replace Ambassador Jose Ignacio Moreno Leon who returns from Canada in September to become rector of the Metropolitan University in Caracas.
There has been no official word or speculation on who might replace Poletto at the FIV.
